For every fixed dimension \(d\ge2\) and every fixed obstacle radius, we construct a sequential importance sampler that is unbiased and asymptotically optimal. The full algorithm has finite expected total work at every fixed horizon, and both its expected work and the coefficient of variation grow at most subexponentially with the time horizon. The method avoids repeatedly solving eigenvalue problems on the evolving explored regions and suits parallel implementation. Numerical experiments illustrate the efficiency of the method.

title: DistFlow and Its Conic Relaxation: Regularity, Monotonicity, and Hybrid Exactness via Graph Decomposition
abstract: Classical exactness conditions for conic relaxations of the DistFlow model rely, among other assumptions, either on all nodal injections being adjustable or on a network-wide path condition. In practice, these conditions may not hold uniformly across a feeder: controllable distributed energy resources (DERs) sit at some buses and fixed loads at others, while reverse flows from DER-rich regions can violate the path condition. This paper certifies exactness region by region and composes the regional certificates, accounting for perturbations that propagate downstream through voltages. We first introduce a subtree voltage stability region, in which the network and all compatible subtrees remain regular. Within it, two endpoint sign conditions, one relaxing the nonnegative-flow assumption and one implied by the classical path condition, yield monotone responses of voltages, currents, and losses to root voltages. Using duality, the implicit function theorem, and sign properties of inverse sensitivity matrices, we recast both classical arguments as individual sign certificates on branch multipliers. This turns exactness into a branchwise property that can be certified region by region. A partition rule then splits the network into dispatchable and passive subtrees, and a hybrid certificate combines their local conditions into exactness of the full-network relaxation, under additional operating-limit and objective conditions. In particular, placing controllable DERs at both ends of a branch with large reverse flow exempts that branch from the passive sign conditions.

title: Local Smoothing Estimates of Schrödinger Operators on Waveguides Using Refined Decoupling
abstract: We establish improved local smoothing estimates for the Schrödinger equation on waveguides. Our results extend the previously known range of exponents in every dimension and are sharp in certain cases. The proof develops a transference argument that preserves the discrete periodic frequency structure, together with a refined decoupling estimate adapted to waveguides. We also derive consequences for Euclidean local smoothing and almost everywhere convergence.

title: Dilation systems with two generators and the optimal Riesz bounds of a basis of ReLU networks
abstract: For two $1$-periodic functions $ψ_1,ψ_2\in L^2(0,1)$ with mean zero we characterize when $\{1\}\cup\{ψ_1(α\cdot x),ψ_2(α\cdot x)\}_{α\in\mathbb{Z}^d,\,α\succ0}$ is a Riesz basis of $L^2([0,1]^d)$, in terms of a $2\times2$ matrix of Dirichlet series, and we compute its optimal bounds. The tool is a $2\times2$ matrix version of the theorem of Hedenmalm, Lindqvist and Seip for systems of dilations with two generators, proved through the reproducing kernel of the Hardy space of the infinite polydisk. In particular, we get the optimal bounds $2/3$ and $3/2$ for $ψ_1,ψ_2$ the triangle waves considered by Daubechies, DeVore, Foucart, Hanin and Petrova in $L^2(0,1)$, and the extended version in $L^2([0,1]^d)$ defined by Schneider and Vybíral.

title: Nonexistence of Stable Solutions to the Liouville Equation on Graphs with Polynomial Volume Growth
abstract: We study stable solutions of the discrete Liouville equation \[ -Δu=e^u \] on infinite, locally finite graphs with polynomial volume growth. We prove that no stable solution exists whenever the order $d$ of polynomial volume growth satisfies $d<10$.

title: Primes and the Möbius function over quadratic polynomials
abstract: We prove an asymptotic formula for the number of primes $p\leq X$ of the form $n^2+h$ for almost all $h \leq X^{1/2-o(1)}$. We prove that, for almost all $h \leq X^{2/5}$, the number of primes satisfies a correct-order lower bound. We also show cancellation of the Möbius function over $n^2+h$ for almost all $h < X^{1/2-o(1)}$.

title: Clique-factors in randomly perturbed hypergraphs
abstract: In this paper we establish the following result for clique-factors in randomly perturbed hypergraphs when the cliques are large enough. For integers $k \geq 3$ and $t\geq t_0(k)$, we show that for every $α> 0$, there exists $C>0$ such that for sufficiently large $n\in(t+1)\mathbb{N}$, the union of a $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices with minimum codegree at least $αn$ and a binomial random $k$-uniform hypergraph $H^{(k)}(n,p)$ with $p\geq Cn^{-{t/\binom{t+1}{k}}}$ on the same vertex set contains a $K_{t+1}^{(k)}$-factor asymptotically almost surely. The bound on $p$ is asymptotically best possible and extends the graph case, resolved by Balogh, Treglown and Wagner. In particular, we have $t_0(3)=3$, which implies that our result applies to every $t\ge 3$ for $3$-uniform hypergraphs. Together with the previously established result for perfect matchings, this covers all possible clique sizes for $3$-uniform hypergraphs.

title: Strongly stable fields
abstract: Let $K$ be a field which is strongly stable, that is, stable and strongly dependent. Then $K$ is finite or algebraically closed. This answers a question of Shelah.

title: On the geometry of asymptotically conical Ricci shrinkers (II): strong uniqueness
abstract: We prove strong uniqueness of tangent flows at the first singular time of a closed Ricci flow when one tangent flow is generated by a complete smooth asymptotically conical Ricci shrinker. The modified flow converges to this shrinker in a fixed gauge, with quantitative estimates on expanding domains. The main ingredients are a Łojasiewicz-Simon inequality for Perelman's entropy, based on the global weighted divergence-free gauge constructed in the preceding paper, and estimates controlling the geometric radius under Ricci flow.

title: A Dual-Guided Column-Generation-Based Matheuristic for Integrated Railroad Blocking
abstract: Integrated railroad blocking is a central planning problem in freight railway operations, which requires coordinated decisions on block design, blocking sequences, and block routing. We propose a dual-guided column-generation-based matheuristic (DG-CGM) that uses linear programming (LP) dual information to identify promising transportation paths and incorporates them into restricted mixed-integer programs to improve feasible solutions. Starting from an initial plan built by construction, DG-CGM alternates destroy and local repair with path generation, which uses dual prices from restricted LPs of a Dantzig-Wolfe reformulation to identify promising transportation paths. When local improvements continue to stagnate, we further apply joint repair to combine alternatives across demand groups. To address the coupling between logical and physical path pricing, we introduce a joint reduced cost that eliminates path-specific dual variables from pricing, enabling more efficient column identification through exact labeling algorithms. We evaluate the performance of DG-CGM on both generated instances and real-world cases. On 150 generated instances with 50-150 nodes, DG-CGM achieves the optimal cost on 89 of the 91 instances solved to proven optimality by Gurobi, with a geometric mean runtime equal to 5.2% of that for Gurobi and a mean relative cost reduction of 3.4%. On six full-scale scenarios derived from the 2026 INFORMS Railway Applications Section competition data, each with 47,193 nodes, DG-CGM obtains feasible solutions within two hours that serve 95.9%-99.6% of the requested freight volume, providing practical blocking plans for large-scale railway operations. The code, instances, and computational results are publicly available at https://github.com/Zhengzhong-You/IRBP.

title: On hot spots of the torsion function and the ground state of the Laplacian
abstract:
We compare the maximum points \(P_Ω\) and \(Q_Ω\) of the
  torsion function and the positive first Dirichlet eigenfunction. We begin with a systematic analytic description of both
  hot spots over the full range of opening angles of circular sectors: uniqueness,
  strict monotonicity with respect to the angle, distinct
  small-angle asymptotics, and explicit limiting equations in the
  slit-disk limit. We also prove the existence of a coincidence angle and establish arithmetic
  properties of the limiting coordinates. We then consider bounded convex planar domains with a line of symmetry, and we prove the sharp diameter-normalized identity
  \[
  \sup_Ω
  \frac{|P_Ω-Q_Ω|}{\operatorname{diam}(Ω)}=\frac12.
  \]
  Its upper-bound argument uses standard localization in the heart and
  an elementary geometric enclosure. Sharpness follows from thin convex
  domains with a vanishing relative width perturbation peaking near one
  endpoint: the torsion hot spot approaches that endpoint, whereas the
  ground-state hot spot approaches the midpoint.

title: Filtration theorems, Hilbert functions, and generic freeness
abstract: Let $M$ be a finitely generated module over a ring $R$ that is a finitely generated algebra over a Noetherian ring $A$ by $r$ elements. We prove that there are finitely many primes $P_1, \ldots, P_k$ of $A$ such that $M$ has a countable ascending filtration by finitely generated $A$-modules with the property that every factor $F_n$ has a filtration by cyclic modules of the form $A/P_i$, $1 \leq i \leq k$ such that the number of copies $H_i(n)$ of $A/P_i$ that occur in the filtration of $F_n$ is an eventually polynomial function of $n$. We prove a number of bounds on the degrees of these eventually polynomial functions: $r-1$ is always a bound, and the dimension of $\dim(M_P)-1$ is a bound under mild hypotheses. One application is an immediate proof Grothedieck's classic theorem on generic freeness. Several other applications are given.

title: Solyanik Estimates for Ergodic Flows
abstract: Let $\{T_t\}_{t\in\mathbb R}$ be a measure-preserving flow on a probability space $(Ω,Σ,μ)$ and let $T^*$ be the associated one-sided ergodic maximal operator. We show that the sharp Tauberian constant $C(α)=\sup_{μ(E)>0}\frac{μ(\{T^*χ_E>α\})}{μ(E)}$,$0<α<1$, equals $1/α$ for every $α\in(0,1)$, unless every measurable set is invariant modulo null sets, in which case $C(α)=1$ for every $α$. In particular the Solyanik estimate $\lim_{α\to1^-}C(α)=1$ holds for every measure-preserving flow, and for ergodic flows on nonatomic spaces the estimate $C(α)-1\le 1/α-1$ holds with equality. This answers the one-parameter case of a question of Hagelstein and Parissis. The main point is the lower bound, which is obtained from a lacunary cross-section built out of the upcrossings of a probe function along the orbits of the flow.

title: Turnpike Properties for Exploratory Stochastic Linear-Quadratic Optimal Control with Indefinite Cost Functionals
abstract: Continuous-time exploratory stochastic control provides a stochastic control framework for the exploration--exploitation trade-off in reinforcement learning. In this paper, we study the long-time behavior of finite-horizon exploratory stochastic linear-quadratic (LQ) optimal control problems as the time horizon $T\to\infty$, and establish so-called turnpike properties for such problems. In the finite-horizon setting, we derive a feedback representation of the exploratory stochastic LQ problem and analyze its long-time structure. We formulate an exploratory static distribution optimization problem analogous to the classical static optimization problem and identify the corresponding static reference object. We prove a turnpike property for the optimal state process relative to a stochastic reference process, as well as a Wasserstein turnpike property for the optimal control distribution. In addition to the exploratory control formulation, another key feature of our results is that, by introducing a joint coercivity condition, we allow the cost functional to be indefinite and the controlled state system to be merely stabilizable. Consequently, the derived turnpike property is novel even within the classical stochastic LQ control framework.

title: Defect TQFTs, the Generalized Cobordism Hypothesis, and Algebraic $K$-Theory
abstract:
By constructing a fully dualizable category $\mathrm{Bord}^{\mathcal{C}}_n$ as the left adjoint of the forgetful functor, we state a generalized cobordism hypothesis. As a corollary, we establish a generalized Pontryagin-Thom isomorphism that gives a geometric interpretation of higher algebraic $K$-theory using cobordism classes of framed manifolds and stratified spaces decorated by categorical string diagrams, which we call lasagnas. For finite-dimensional vector spaces over a field, these decorations are branched local systems.
  We also examine low-dimensional representatives, including $K_1$, Steinberg-group presentations of $K_2$, and fillings related to the Steinberg relation, providing a more explicit construction of Ghys' manifold.

title: Semipositivity and complete subvarieties of projectivised strata of holomorphic differentials
abstract: We show that if the projectivised stratum $\mathbb{P}{H}_g(μ)$ associated to a partition $μ=(m_1,\ldots,m_n)$ of $2g-2$ contains a complete curve, then \[ κ_μ:=\sum_{i=1}^n\frac{m_i(m_i+2)}{m_i+1}>12. \] The weak inequality follows from semipositivity applied to a quotient of the Hodge bundle, while equality is excluded using the second Fujita decomposition and the geometry of fibred surfaces with maximal unitary rank. Consequently, no projectivised holomorphic stratum in genus $g\leq5$ contains a positive-dimensional complete subvariety. In genus $g=6$ the same conclusion holds for \[ (10),\ (9,1),\ (8,2),\ (8,1,1),\ (7,3),\ (6,4),\ (5,5). \]

title: Equivariant Ehrhart series for rational simplices and rational cross-polytopes
abstract:
Equivariant Ehrhart theory was introduced by Stapledon (2011) and has since been extensively studied. A central question is whether the numerator in a certain rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series is both a polynomial and effective.
  In this paper, we propose a modification of the denominator in the rational function expression for the equivariant Ehrhart series of rational polytopes. For rational simplices and rational cross-polytopes whose vertices have coordinates that are reciprocals of integers, we show that the resulting numerator is a polynomial and is effective. As an application of our results, we compute the equivariant series of the characteristic quasi-polynomials of root systems.

title: Robust Principal Component Analysis via $\ell_0$ Alternating Minimization
abstract: Robust principal component analysis concerns the recovery of a low-rank matrix $Z$ and a sparse matrix $S$ from their observed sum $D = Z + S$. In this paper, we study this recovery problem under an $\ell_0$ sparsity penalty and a rank constraint on the low-rank component. By exploiting the entrywise separable structure of the sparse subproblem, we obtain an exact closed-form solution via hard thresholding with box clipping, avoiding the shrinkage bias of $\ell_1$-based methods. The low-rank subproblem is solved by truncated SVD. We prove block-coordinate convergence of the resulting alternating minimization scheme, establish uniqueness of block minimizers under non-degeneracy and singular value gap conditions, establish local linear convergence under a contraction condition on the Fréchet derivative of the truncated SVD operator restricted to the sparse support, and provide a second-order optimality analysis via the Riemannian Hessian. Experiments on synthetic data, images, and video show that the proposed algorithm outperforms the existing convex and nonconvex algorithms, most notably in support recovery and in the accuracy-efficiency trade-off.

title: Tracy Widom law for sample covariance matrices under quadratic form concentration
abstract: We study sample covariance matrices formed from i.i.d., centered, isotropic random vectors $q_1, \dots, q_N \in \mathbb{R}^M$, whose coordinates are allowed to be dependent. We assume the random vectors satisfy a concentration bound for their quadratic forms $q_i^T A q_i$. Under this assumption, we establish edge universality and obtain the Tracy--Widom law for the largest eigenvalue of the sample covariance matrix after appropriate centering and scaling. In particular, our result removes the unconditionality assumption in existing edge universality results for log-concave ensembles~\cite{BX}, resolving the question that originally motivated our work. The concentration assumption also allows us to extend the result beyond the log-concave class.

title: Twisted second moments of Dirichlet $L$-functions with applications to weighted one-level density
abstract: We give an asymptotic formula for the twisted second moment of a fixed Dirichlet $L$-function in the $t$-aspect. This is a generalization of Selberg's asymptotic formula for the twisted second moment of the Riemann zeta function. As an application, we observe the change and the stability of the weighted one-level density of zeros of a fixed Dirichlet $L$-function.

title: New results on openly disjoint cycles in regular digraphs
abstract: Given a digraph \(D\), let \(c(D)\) be the largest size of a collection of openly disjoint directed cycles through a common vertex, and let \(c_r\) be the minimum of \(c(D)\) over all \(r\)-regular digraphs \(D\). In 2005, Seymour asked whether every \(r\)-regular digraph satisfies \(c(D)=r\). Mader answered Seymour's problem negatively for every \(r\ge 8\), but conjectured that nevertheless \(\lim_{r\to\infty}c_r=\infty\). Recently, Steiner confirmed this conjecture by proving \[ \left\lceil \frac{3r}{22}\right\rceil \le c_r \le 7\left\lceil \frac{r}{8}\right\rceil. \] In this paper, we first answer Seymour's problem negatively for $r\in \{6,7\}$, and then improve Steiner's bound to \[ \left\lceil \frac{r}{6}\right\rceil \le c_r \le 5\left\lceil \frac{r}{6}\right\rceil.\]

title: Disconnectedness of stability manifolds and their geometric loci, and separation of braid orbits of semiorthogonal decompositions
abstract: This paper proves that the Bridgeland stability manifold $\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ has infinitely many connected components for general quintic threefolds, other general complete intersection Calabi--Yau threefolds, certain odd-dimensional Calabi--Yau varieties, and certain rational weak Fano varieties. Moreover, we show that the geometric locus $\mathrm{Stab}^{\mathrm{geo}}(X)$ meets distinct connected components of $\mathrm{Stab}(X)$ for general quintic threefolds and their products with varieties with finite Albanese morphisms, which gives examples in any dimension at least three. For the weak Fano examples, we also construct semiorthogonal decompositions in infinitely many braid group orbits. The proof is an extension of Nordskova's argument to families, using semilinear autoequivalences and absolute Galois actions on geometric generic fibers to permute mutually orthogonal spherical objects. Then, we specialize the separation to closed fibers. In our examples, the spherical objects are constructed from rigid rational curves or spinor bundles on quadrics.

title: Integral Harnack-type estimates and the rate of extinction for nonlocal doubly nonlinear parabolic equations
abstract: We establish local boundedness and integral Harnack-type inequalities for locally nonnegative weak solutions to nonlocal doubly nonlinear parabolic equations in the fast diffusion range by combining refined energy estimates with a careful treatment of the nonlocal terms. As an application, quantitative decay estimates for both the local mass and the local supremum of weak solutions are derived near the extinction time. Furthermore, we study the extinction phenomenon for bounded nonnegative weak solutions to the Cauchy--Dirichlet problem and obtain quantitative upper bounds for the extinction time.

title: Sparse descent subspace-Newton thresholding algorithm for sparse optimization problems
abstract: In this paper, we propose a sparse descent direction derived from the Newton direction within a low-dimensional subspace for sparse optimization problems. Building upon this direction and incorporating hard thresholding and orthogonal projection, we develop a novel algorithm termed the sparse descent subspace-Newton thresholding (SDSNT) algorithm. We further establish its global convergence under the restricted isometry property $δ_{3k}\leq \sqrt{3/20}$ of the measurement matrix. Numerical experiments on random sparse vector recovery and audio signal reconstruction reveal that SDSNT achieves comparable performance to several state-of-the-art algorithms. Notably, relative to most of them, it delivers superior recovery at high sparsity levels and improved efficiency at low sparsity levels.

title: Pebbling Numbers and Generator Reinforcement of Cayley Graphs
abstract: We study inverse-closed generator additions of minimum size that make the optimal pebbling number of a finite Cayley graph at most three while preserving its specified regular action. A weighted vertex-cover formulation on inverse orbits yields an $O(|Γ|^2)$ algorithm for abelian groups in the explicit multiplication-table model. We derive formulas for central involutions and cubelike graphs, with an inverse-closure correction determined by square roots in the uncovered set. The exact thresholds are $2^{d-1}-d$ for hypercubes ($d\ge1$), and $3$ for standard Keller graphs when $d=2$ and $2^{d-1}$ when $d\ge3$. Every admissible augmentation of either family has ordinary pebbling number equal to its order.

title: RapidDOC: Riccati-Preconditioned Implicit Differentiation for Differentiable Optimal Control under Operator Mismatch
abstract: Differentiable optimal control embeds constrained optimization problems in data-driven pipelines by differentiating their optimality conditions and propagating task-loss gradients to model or objective parameters. A key observation is that forward optimization and backward sensitivity computation involve related stage-structured linear systems, making reuse of forward factorization information natural. However, direct reuse is generally invalid, because differences in linearization, barrier terms, regularization, and curvature can create a mismatch between the retained forward operator and the target operator defining the derivative. We therefore propose RapidDOC, a factorization-reuse method that leaves the target adjoint equation unchanged. The retained cache produces a candidate adjoint and, when its target residual exceeds the prescribed tolerance, serves as a fixed right preconditioner for GMRES. A cache-action error operator characterizes directional exactness, the preconditioned iteration, and the relation between target residual and outer-gradient error. An ablation on three constrained robotic OCPs shows that the proposed method achieves lower backward time than both target-system refactorization and a no-reuse iterative method, demonstrating the computational benefit of reusing the retained forward factorizations. Across open- and closed-loop parameter-learning experiments, the proposed method achieves learning performance comparable to the baselines, while yielding the lowest open-loop backward time on all three tasks and reducing total closed-loop solver-call time by 40.5-83.1% relative to the fastest competing method. Finally, deploying the learned controller on a physical vehicle reduces the median figure-eight tracking RMSE from 22.75 to 6.09 cm, demonstrating its potential for hardware deployment.

title: Invariant probability measures for path-dependent regime-switching processes
abstract: We consider stochastic functional differential equations with Markovian regime?switching on an (infinitely) countable state space. Via establishing the Feller prop?erty and contraction in L1-Wasserstein distance of the semigroup associated with the segment process, we show the existence and uniqueness of invariant probability measure. In order to cope with switching processes on an infinite state space, we de?velop a truncation method based on a new construction of order preserving coupling for Markov chains to generalize the estimation of exponential functionals for Markov chains with infinite states. The existing sharp estimation is only valid for Markov chains on a finite state space, as it fundamentally relies on the Perron-Frobenius theorem.

title: A well-balanced path-conservative discontinuous Galerkin method with generalized hydrostatic reconstruction for non-conservative balance laws
abstract: We propose a high-order well-balanced path-conservative discontinuous Galerkin method for one-dimensional balance laws with non-conservative products. Generalized hydrostatic reconstruction at cell interfaces couples effective numerical fluxes with Dal Maso-LeFloch-Murat path integrals, while a cellwise reference-equilibrium decomposition cancels projection-induced residuals in the volume discretization. Under explicit assumptions on equilibrium recovery, admissibility, paths, and boundary data, the spatial discretization is path conservative, and prescribed rest and moving equilibria are exactly preserved by both the semi-discrete scheme and its fully discrete SSP-RK approximation. The framework is applied to the two-layer shallow water equations and a blood-flow model with spatially varying vessel properties. Numerical experiments confirm the designed order of accuracy and round-off-level preservation of smooth and discontinuous equilibria, demonstrate accurate resolution of small perturbations, and show that the interface treatment captures shocks and stationary material contacts without visible spurious oscillations.

title: A local-to-global fixed point theorem for $\CAT(0)$ spaces with a uniform elliptic gap
abstract: A finitely generated group acting locally elliptically on a complete \CAT(0) space of finite geometric dimension fixes a point if distances to elliptic fixed sets are uniformly controlled by displacements. For arbitrary groups, the same hypothesis gives a fixed point in the space or its visual boundary. The proof combines a first-moment random-walk displacement estimate with Izeki's zero-drift theorem. For finite-rank $\R$-buildings whose Euclidean metric factor has finite linear image, we obtain an all-type local-to-global theorem, including the nondiscrete $\widetilde G_2$ case, with an explicit gap and without metric completeness; the linear-image restriction can be removed from the fixed-point conclusion when the Euclidean factor has dimension at most three. A tangent-cone criterion characterizes the gap and yields a cubical bound with optimal asymptotic growth $d/π$ in dimension $d$. For Hadamard manifolds, the gap is equivalent to uniformly bounded finite stabilizers in the isometry image, with stabilizer bounds of optimal polynomial growth in the gap constant.

title: Fock Projections between Gaussian Mixed-Norm Spaces: Full-Range Boundedness and Compactness
abstract: The Fock--Bargmann projection \(P_t\) is initially an orthogonal projection on a Gaussian Hilbert space. We characterize the boundedness and compactness of \[ P_t:L_α^{p_1,q_1}\longrightarrow \mathcal F_β^{p_2,q_2} \] and of its associated maximal projection \[ P_t^+:L_α^{p_1,q_1}\longrightarrow L_β^{p_2,q_2} \] for all \(t,α,β>0\) and \(0<p_1,q_1,p_2,q_2\le\infty\). Set \[ Δ(t;α,β):=t^2-2βt+αβ, \qquad d(p,q):=\frac1q-\frac1p. \] For both operators, boundedness holds exactly when \(p_1,q_1\ge1\) and either \(Δ(t;α,β)<0\), or \(Δ(t;α,β)=0\) with \[ q_1\le q_2, \qquad d(p_2,q_2)\le d(p_1,q_1). \] Both operators are compact exactly when \(p_1,q_1\ge1\) and either \(Δ(t;α,β)<0\), or \(Δ(t;α,β)=0\) with both of the above boundary inequalities strict. Thus boundedness forces the source exponents into the Banach range, whereas when \(Δ(t;α,β)<0\), every target exponent is admissible, including quasi-Banach ones. Annular discretization reduces the problem to drifted Gaussian sequence operators, whose comparison with diagonal sequence operators yields the endpoint criteria and quantitative tail estimates. A dilation--multiplier transfer gives corresponding results for Gaussian-twisted Fock operators, including Berezin transforms.

title: Ullman--Stahl--Totik regularity for conjugacy measures
abstract: We consider probability measures whose distribution functions solve conjugate equations between two compatible systems of increasing maps on the unit interval. We give sufficient conditions for Ullman--Stahl--Totik regularity in terms of finite compositions of the source maps and a lower mass estimate which holds at Lebesgue almost every point. Our result substantially extends a regularity theorem of Mantica and Totik by allowing nonlinear target maps and replacing their assumptions on convexity, concavity, and displacement near fixed points. The proof uses the mass criterion of Stahl and Totik from logarithmic potential theory. We give further sufficient conditions involving uniform mesh bounds, sets where derivatives equal one, and endpoint drift. Examples distinguish these conditions and show that the uniform version of the lower mass estimate can fail for regular conjugacy measures.

title: Infeasible Momentum Orthogonalized Methods for Optimization on the Stiefel Manifold
abstract: We study deterministic and stochastic optimization over the Stiefel manifold, explicitly allowing iterates to deviate from the manifold rather than enforcing feasibility via retraction at each step. We introduce Landom, a Landing-type method that constructs momentum in the relative-gradient direction, maps this update to its compact polar factor, and combines the resulting tangential step with a step along the negative gradient of the orthogonality penalty to improve feasibility. Under operator-to-nuclear smoothness, Landom achieves an $O(T^{-1/2})$ bound on the averaged nuclear norm of the relative gradient with exact gradients, and an $O(T^{-1/4})$ bound in expectation with stochastic momentum, bounded variance, and a fixed batch size. Our analysis also provides explicit pathwise bounds on the orthogonality residual, including its dependence on the step size and initial infeasibility. To address the coupling between objective and feasibility correction in Landom, we further propose Landom+, a two-timescale variant in which the tangential and normal step sizes are decoupled. By keeping the normal step size fixed, Landom+ achieves tighter control over the orthogonality residual following an initial transient while maintaining the respective convergence rates for stationarity. Numerical experiments across a range of applications illustrate that the proposed algorithms remain competitive with established manifold optimization approaches.

title: The lattice of antichains of intervals: Dyck paths, level sets, and sweep dimension
abstract: The Clarke-Cormack-Burkowski lattice $\mathcal{E}_n$ is the lattice of antichains of intervals of the chain $\{0,1,\dots,n-1\}$, the algebraic structure underlying minimal-interval semantics, a query semantics used in information retrieval. We give an explicit, elementary anti-isomorphism between $\mathcal{E}_n$ minus its top element and the Stanley lattice of Dyck words of semilength $n+1$ (an anti-isomorphism whose existence is implicit in work of Ferrari and Munarini), under which the rank of an antichain is $\binom{n+1}{2}$ minus the area of the associated Dyck word. Hence the rank generating function of $\mathcal{E}_n\setminus\{\top\}$ is the reverse of the Carlitz-Riordan $q$-Catalan polynomial. Using a local limit theorem for the area of random-walk excursions, we confirm unconditionally an asymptotic formula of Takács: the size $λ_n$ of the largest level set of $\mathcal{E}_n$ satisfies $λ_n\simκ\,4^{n+1}/(n+1)^3$, where $κ\approx1.0807$. Finally, for the antichains of intervals of an arbitrary finite poset $P$ we study the sweep dimension, the minimum number of linear orders needed to separate every interval from every element outside it. It equals the Dushnik-Miller dimension of the lattice of convex subsets of $P$, it is the least $k$ for which $P$ maps into $\mathbb{R}^k$ so that every interval is the preimage of an upper orthant, and it lies between $\max(2,w)$ and $2w$, where $w$ is the width of $P$, both bounds being tight. Antichains of intervals embed, preserving joins, into $k$-dimensional staircase regions.

title: Two-coloring the points of a projective plane
abstract: Let us color the points of a projective plane of odd order $n$ with two colors, say red and blue. Erdős asked the question of determining the maximum number of balanced lines (that have the same number of red and blue points). The answer is $n^2$, and in the corresponding trivial coloring the unbalanced lines go through a point. In this paper, we consider the Galois plane $\mathrm{PG}(2,q)$ and determine the number of unbalanced lines for a non-trivial coloring. The problem can also be generalized to $(r,b)$-colored lines (see Definition 1.1) and in many cases we extend the results to the generalized problem. Our strongest result for Galois planes of prime order $p$ describes all 2-colorings with at most $\max\{3p+1,4p-22\}$ not $(r,b)$-colored lines (see Theorem 5.13). Finally, in case of the generalized problem, we allow even more not $(r,b)$-colored lines if $r$ is small and the order is prime (for more details, see Theorem 5.18).

title: A Model for Fast Mining Blockchains
abstract: We study a Markovian model for a blockchain mining process. In the limit where there is an infinite number of miners, the model satisfies a functional law of large numbers due to Barbour and Luczac (2008), leading to an infinite set of coupled ODEs characterising the blockchain heights. We show that the sequence of solutions to this system converges uniformly, to a limiting profile in an appropriate comoving frame. Utilising asymptotic arguments inspired by Brunet and Derrida (1997), we derive an explicit expression for the position of the travelling front, which exhibits a leading order logarithmic Bramson correction in time. For a finite number of miners, we further derive a correction to the travelling speed which is logarithmic in the number of miners. Finally, by application of a computation due to Ablowitz and Zeppetella (1979), we identify that, for a specific choice of the travelling speed, the Painlevé integrable, travelling wave solution of the Fisher-KPP equation with drift accurately matches our limiting profile. Our results are supported by numerical simulations.

title: Vector Valued Katok-Sarnak Formulas
abstract: We introduce a version of the Katok-Sarnak formula linking twisted traces of scalar valued Maass cusp forms for $Γ_0(N)$ with $N$ square-free to Fourier coefficients of vector valued Maass cusp forms for the metaplectic group $\operatorname{Mp}_2(\mathbb{Z})$ and the Weil representation associated to a lattice of signature $(2,1)$. We prove this by computing the Fourier coefficients of the vector valued Siegel and Millson theta lift of a scalar valued newform by two different methods and comparing the results.

title: Strong solvability and its failure for critical SDEs
abstract:
We revisit the construction of strong solutions to singular SDEs by compactness on Wiener space. For spatially varying diffusion coefficients, assuming sufficiently small form bounds on the drift and diffusion gradient, we use basic energy estimates and an extended compactness criterion for Wiener functionals to construct an approximation-independent stochastic flow of homeomorphisms. Both forward and inverse maps have local Sobolev moment bounds, and the resulting strong solutions are pathwise unique in a class of solutions satisfying a Krylov estimate.
  We also show that the endpoint critical condition $b\in L^\infty_tL^d_x$, together with $\mathrm{div } b=0$ does not guarantee the existence of a strong solution. For every $d\geq2$, we construct a SDE with a divergence-free drift in this class and an additive Brownian noise, started from the origin, has a weak solution unique in law, but no strong solution. The proof uses logarithmic rescaling to characterize strong solvability by whether the sample measures of an associated stationary diffusion are Dirac masses. Positivity of the top Lyapunov exponent, combined with random SRB theory, rules out this concentration and hence strong solvability.

title: Deck Reconstruction for Restricted Word Classes
abstract:
For a binary word $x\in \{0,1\}^+$, the $k$-deck of $x$ is the multiset of all length-$k$ subsequences counted with multiplicity. The deck reconstruction problem asks for the minimum $k$ such that every word of a fixed length is uniquely determined by its $k$-deck. In this paper, we study deck reconstruction for several restricted classes of binary words, including words with exactly $s$ ones, words with at most $\ell$ runs of ones, and words where the indices of ones are given by a monotone polynomial of degree $d$. We prove that for these classes of words, their reconstruction thresholds are bounded by a function of the structural complexity of the class.
  We also study weak deck reconstruction, in which subwords may contain "wildcard" symbols that map to either 0 or 1. By generalizing a "template lemma" of Dudík and Schulman, we improve the upper bound in an open question about weak reconstruction from Dudík and Schulman. Finally, for the class of periodic words with period $d$, we prove that its in-class reconstruction threshold is equal to the general reconstruction threshold for words of length $d$, and give a general template construction producing further classes with the same threshold-preservation phenomenon.

title: A note on decompositions into 3-chromatic graphs
abstract: Delcourt and Postle recently introduced the `discharging in the dual' proof technique, leading to a breakthrough proof of Nash-Williams' conjecture on triangle decompositions. Independently, and almost simultaneously, the first and second authors built on the `condensation' method of Bryant, Dukes, Horsley, Maenhaut and Montgomery to determine the decomposition threshold of all odd cycles of length at least $73$. In this note, we explain how the `discharging in the dual' and `condensation' methods can be combined to determine the decomposition threshold of cycles of any odd length, as well as the approximate decomposition threshold of a range of other $3$-chromatic graphs.

title: Discrete total variation under the multinomial, Part 3: expectation under a general distribution
abstract: For multinomial counts $X\sim\operatorname{Mult}(N;\mathbf p)$ on $n$ ordered bins and a reference law $\mathbf r$ we study the expectation of the reference-centered discrete total variation $d_{\mathbf r}(X)=\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}|(X_{j+1}-Nr_{j+1})-(X_j-Nr_j)|$, the natural extension of the comb-test statistic to a non-uniform null. For a non-uniform null the raw total variation of the counts carries a deterministic staircase of order $N$ that no centering of the statistic removes; the counts are therefore centered at the reference law, and under the null ($\mathbf p=\mathbf r$) the statistic is the matched $d_{\mathbf p}$. Exact finite-sample expectations are obtained by conditioning on the total mass in each adjacent pair, which reduces every edge to a translated binomial absolute-deviation problem. For fixed $n\ge3$ and a sampling law bounded away from the boundary of the simplex, the matched statistic admits a three-term asymptotic expansion in powers of $1/N$ whose coefficients are explicit continuous periodic functions of $N(p_{j+1}-p_j)$ (a generalized, non-Poincaré asymptotic expansion), obtained by a weighted local Edgeworth estimate and a corner Euler--Maclaurin summation; all half-integer orders vanish by parity. Each correction separates into a smooth Edgeworth part and an oscillatory lattice part, the latter an Edgeworth perturbation of one formal Euler--Maclaurin series of a Gaussian lattice sum. Under a sampling law $\mathbf p\neq\mathbf r$ the leading expectation is the folded-normal profile implied by the central limit theorem; under local alternatives we identify the $O(1)$ correction (a skewness term, plus a variance-gradient term for Pitman alternatives), and fixed alternatives give a law-of-large-numbers limit, the $\ell_1$ distance between the adjacent-gradient profiles of $\mathbf p$ and $\mathbf r$, on which threshold tests are consistent.

title: Odd-Degree Rigidity and a Numerical Characterization of Complete Flag Varieties
abstract:
Let $F=G/B$ be the complete flag variety of a connected semisimple complex linear algebraic group. We prove that if a smooth Fano variety $X$ has the same dimension and Picard number as $F$, then the existence of a continuous map $X\to F$ of odd topological degree implies $X$ is isomorphic to $F$. In particular, a smooth Fano variety homotopy equivalent to $F$ is isomorphic to $F$.
  The algebraic input is a numerical characterization of complete flags: a positive-dimensional smooth Fano variety $X$ is a complete flag variety if and only if its pseudoindex $ι_X$ is at least two and ${\rm ker}({\rm Sym}^2N^1(X)_{\mathbb R}\to N^2(X)_{\mathbb R})$ contains a positive-definite quadratic form. The pseudoindex condition can equivalently be replaced by the divisibility of $-K_X$ by two in ${\rm Pic}(X)$. The key observation is that a single definite quadratic relation excludes surfaces in every fiber of any elementary contraction; standard contraction theorems then yield smooth ${\mathbb P}^1$-fibrations and the characterization of complete flags applies. For the odd-degree theorem, Poincaré duality and a mod-two Wu-class argument show that the anticanonical class is divisible by two; comparison of the integral coroot lattices then identifies the flag. Most proofs were developed through extensive discussions with OpenAI's ChatGPT (GPT-5.6 Sol and GPT-6), based on mathematical directions supplied by the author and arguments suggested by ChatGPT; see the AI Disclosure.

title: Rainbow Hamiltonian paths in graph collections under edge-size conditions
abstract: Let $\mathbf{G}=\{G_1,\dots,G_{n-1}\}$ be a collection of not necessarily distinct graphs of order $n$ on the same vertex set $V$. A path $P$ with $V(P)\subseteq V$ is called \emph{rainbow} in $\mathbf{G}$, if there exists an injection $φ\colon E(P)\to [n-1]$ such that $e\in E(G_{φ(e)})$ for each $e\in E(P)$. In this paper, we show that if $n\ge3$, $e(G_i)> \binom{n-2}{2}+2$ for each $i\in[n-1]$ and $G_j$ is connected for some $j\in[n-1]$, then there exists a rainbow Hamiltonian path in $\mathbf{G}$ unless $n=6$ with $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{5}\cong K_2\vee 4K_1$, or $n=8$ with $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{7}\cong K_3\vee 5K_1$. This corrects Theorem 6 in [Graphs Combin., \textbf{41}(6)(2025), 119] and relaxes its hypothesis from requiring all $G_i$ to be connected to only requiring that at least one $G_i$ is connected, where $i\in[n-1]$. Moreover, we show that if $n\ge2$ and $e(G_i)\ge \binom{n-1}{2}$ for each $i\in[n-1]$, then $\mathbf{G}$ contains a rainbow Hamiltonian path unless $G_1=G_2=\dots=G_{n-1}\cong K_{n-1}\cup K_1$, or $n=4$ with $G_1=G_2=G_3\cong K_{1,3}$. As a consequence, Theorem 2 of [Discrete Math., \textbf{347}(2024), 114128] follows immediately.

title: Algebraic Vector Fields of Connected Semi-simple Matrix Groups are 3-generated
abstract: We show that the Lie algebra of algebraic vector fields for any connected, semi-simple matrix group over $\mathbb{F}$, for $\mathbb{F}=\mathbb{R},\mathbb{C}$, can be generated by three $\mathbb{F}$-complete algebraic vector fields.

title: Changing parameters in Hall-Littlewood functions
abstract: We study the transition coefficients $b_{λ,μ}(q,t)$ of the Hall--Littlewood $P$-functions $P_λ(t)$ expanded in the basis $P_μ(q)$. We find a tableaux formula when $λ$ is a hook shape which generalizes term-by-term Lascoux-Schutzenberger's charge formula as well as Macdonald's monomial expansion formula for Hall-Littlewood functions. We conjecture that $b_{λ,μ}(t+1,t)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}[t]$ and prove it when $λ$ is a hook shape, when $λ$ has two-columns and some more simple cases. We prove that $b_{λ,μ}(t+n,n)\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}[t]$ for every $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}$, extending work of Alexandersson, and we record a stability property and some reduction principles.

title: Critical fluctuations in the edge--triangle exponential random graph models
abstract: We prove quantitative limit theorems for the edge density $Q$ in the dense edge--triangle exponential random graph model at criticality and under parameter perturbations of order $n^{-1}$. At the fixed critical parameters $(α_c,h_c),$ the centered fluctuations satisfy $n^{2/3}(Q-\mathbb{E} Q)\Rightarrow \mathcal{N}(0,σ_0^2)$, with explicit variance $σ_0^2>0$. This disproves the quartic fluctuation conjecture of Bianchi, Collet and Magnanini (2024). Gaussian limits also hold $(α_c+ λ/n,h_c + γ/n)$, except when the coefficients satisfy $-\frac{11}{16}+\frac{2}{9}(γ+\frac49λ)=0$. Under this linearity condition, the limiting laws of $\sqrt n(Q-2/3)$ have densities proportional to $\exp\{-81z^4/64+9θz^2/8\}$, where $θ=-57/16+8λ/27$. We obtain a sharp $n^{-1/3}$ rate in $1$-Wasserstein distance for the Gaussian limits and an $O(n^{-1/2})$ bound for the quartic limits. The proofs combine Stein's method for exchangeable pairs with conditional row estimates and a local Dobrushin contraction.

title: Bounds on the maximum denominator of fractional chromatic numbers
abstract: For a positive rational number $x=p/q$, where $p$ and $q$ are coprime positive integers, let $\operatorname{den}(x)=q$. For a positive integer $n$, let $\operatorname{sd}(n)=\max\{\operatorname{den}(χ_f(G)): |V(G)|=n\}$. Let $D(n)=2^{-n}(n+1)^{(n+1)/2}$. It was proved by Alon, Tuza and Voigt that $\operatorname{sd}(n)\le D(n)$. In this paper, we prove that $\operatorname{sd}(n)\le D(n)n^{-\frac12\log_2 n+\frac14\log_2\log_2 n+O(1)}$ for all sufficiently large $n$. For the lower bound on $\operatorname{sd}(n)$, it was recently proved by Bonamy, Hylasová, Kaiser and Sereni that $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{sd}(n)^{1/n}\ge\sqrt{2}$. We prove that $\limsup_{n\to\infty}\operatorname{sd}(n)^{1/n}\ge 3^{1/3}>\sqrt{2}$.

title: On the generic case of Jiang's conjecture
abstract: Jiang's conjecture predicts that if $π$ is a generic representation of a quasi-split $p$-adic group, then the $L$-parameter of the Aubert-Zelevinsky involution of $π$ must be trivial on $\mathrm{SL}_2$. In this paper, we prove this statement for a general quasi-split group under certain assumptions on the conjectural local Langlands correspondence.

title: CRCs in four-dimensional lattice graphs
abstract: We obtain series of new completely regular codes in Cayley graphs of the groups $Z_q^n$ with the Lee metric. Combined with binary linear programming methods, the constructions lead to enumeration of all completely regular codes in such graphs for the groups $Z_q^4$, $q\leq 7$ up to parameter matrices.

title: Exchange graphs and $g$-vectors of surface rigid algebras
abstract: We classify the connected components of support $τ$-tilting graphs of surface rigid algebras associated with partial tagged triangulations of punctured marked surfaces with nonempty boundary. For a connected algebra, the graph is disconnected if and only if the algebra is weakly symmetric, has at least two simple modules, and has Cartan rank one. In this case, it has exactly two connected components. For every nonzero $τ$-rigid pair over a connected surface rigid algebra, the graph of $τ$-tilting completions is connected. More generally, we classify the completion components for an arbitrary surface rigid algebra and a fixed $τ$-rigid pair. For partial tagged triangulations with all endpoints at punctures, we express the Cartan matrix and $g$-vectors by signed endpoint data. We prove that $τ$-tilting finiteness is equivalent to positive definiteness of the Cartan matrix. In the finite case, we determine the primitive $g$-vector ray generators in endpoint coordinates. Trees give type A, and a criterion on the original partial tagged triangulation distinguishes types D and C in the unicyclic case.

title: Secure Deterministic Identification with Feedback and Sensing over State-Dependent Wiretap Channels
abstract:
Identification differs from classical transmission in that the receiver determines whether a particular identity was sent rather than recovering a message. We study secure deterministic identification over state-dependent discrete memoryless wiretap channels with private noiseless feedback and a sensing distortion constraint. The encoder has no local randomness and uses only the identity and past feedback. A symbol-wise input restriction guarantees the sensing constraint.
  We show that the secure deterministic identification capacity equals its non-secure feedback counterpart when the admissible main channel has positive ordinary transmission capacity and H(Y|Z,X=x)>0 for some fixed admissible input x. This equality does not require positive classical wiretap secrecy capacity. For achievability, noiseless feedback generates common randomness for identification and enables secret-key extraction by privacy amplification. The extracted key one-time-pad encrypts a short identification tag, whose reliable transmission requires only a sublinear number of additional channel uses. We also present an alternative construction in which feedback-generated randomness replaces the local randomization of a stochastic wiretap encoder.
  We further prove that secure identification capacity vanishes whenever non-secure identification capacity is zero. We also identify a class of channels with input-independent wiretapper observations that achieves full non-secure identification capacity even when the private conditional feedback entropy is zero, illustrated by a binary state-dependent wiretap channel. Thus, feedback can support both identification and secrecy without local encoder randomization while satisfying sensing constraints.

title: A Gaussian Process Regression-Enhanced Two-Sweep Parameterized Power Method for Computing Extreme Eigenpairs
abstract: For computing the dominant eigenvalue and the corresponding eigenvector of a real and symmetric matrix, inspired by the parameterized power method and multistep iteration, we propose a two-sweep parameterized power method, and establish its convergence theory. To further improve the convergence speed of the new method, we use Gaussian process regression (GPR) to predict the quasi-optimal parameter and give a version of the proposed method based on GPR. Numerical experiments show that the two-sweep parameterized power method with quasi-optimal parameters outperforms some existing methods in terms of computing efficiency.

title: Quasi-projective dimensions over homological ring epimorphisms
abstract: In this paper, we study quasi-projective dimensions of modules over rings connected by homological ring epimorphisms. We establish several inequalities relating the quasi-projective dimensions over the source and target rings. As applications, we investigate the quasi-global dimension of triangular matrix rings and provide examples showing that the class of modules with finite quasi-projective dimension does not satisfy the 2-out-of-3 property in general.

title: Joint universality of the Riemann zeta-function with arbitrary real shift parameters
abstract: We prove that the shifts $ζ(s+id_jτ)$, $1\le j\le n$, are jointly universal for any nonzero real parameters $d_j$ with pairwise distinct absolute values. These restrictions are best possible. As an immediate consequence, we obtain generalized strong recurrence for arbitrary finite families of nonzero real parameters. Our proof uses Emsalem's generalization of the six exponentials theorem and a new variant of Pecherskii's rearrangement theorem.

title: Extended Tropical Characteristic Fibers and Slopes of Binomial D-Modules
abstract: For a holonomic $D$-module, we consider the extended tropicalization of the reduced $L$-characteristic fiber along the family $L_s=F+(s-1)V_Y$. For $A$-hypergeometric systems, this tropical fiber determines the complete $(A,L)$-umbrella and hence recovers the classical slopes. We extend this result to holonomic binomial $D$-modules, for which the tropical jump parameters are exactly the classical slopes at the origin. As an application, a holonomic binomial $D$-module is regular holonomic if and only if there are no tropical jumps along any coordinate subspace.

title: Perfect state transfer on unicyclic graphs
abstract: We characterize adjacency perfect state transfer in connected unicyclic graphs: the transfer vertices are opposite degree-two vertices of a four-cycle, and the two attached trees satisfy a characteristic-polynomial condition. Except for the four-cycle, the transfer pair is unique and the minimum transfer time is $π/\sqrt2$. Outside the four-cycle, we obtain sharp lower bounds of $46$ on the order and $10$ on the maximum degree, and classify all examples of maximum degree at most $20$. A finite inverse construction enumerates all realizations of a prescribed eigenvalue support at the transfer vertices. For supports of size at least seven, we establish the sharp maximum-degree lower bound of $21$. Every seven-element support $\{0,\pm\sqrt2,\pm u\sqrt2,\pm v\sqrt2\}$, with odd integers $3\leq u<v$, is realizable, and every such realization has attachment depth at most four. Explicit branching rules give a minimum-order recurrence. Among all connected unicyclic graphs admitting perfect state transfer with seven-element eigenvalue support, the minimum order is $218$, attained uniquely up to isomorphism.

title: On sign patterns of Fourier coefficients of theta quotients
abstract: Motivated by conjectures of Schlosser and Zhou on sign patterns of Fourier coefficients of infinite products, we study two families of theta quotients and their positive integral powers. We determine asymptotic formulas for their Fourier coefficients and use them to obtain explicit eventual periodic sign patterns. Our results provide new instances of the sign phenomena observed by Schlosser and Zhou and illustrate how dominant cusps determine the resulting sign patterns. These results were formalized and verified in Lean by AxiomProver.

title: The role of symmetry in the performance of the Thresholding Greedy Algorithm
abstract: This paper continues the study of conditional symmetric systems initiated in arXiv:2601.15784 and solves several problems posed there. While the interaction between unconditionality and symmetry is well known in the Banach setting following the work in arXiv:2304.05888 and arXiv:2601.15784, we broaden the scope and address similar questions for spreading systems in the more general setting of quasi-Banach spaces. Our aim is twofold. On the one hand, we characterize which spreading systems of Banach spaces are unconditional. On the other hand, we provide examples of quasi-Banach spaces equipped with conditional systems with symmetry-related properties to illustrate the connections between symmetry, greedy-like properties, and the Schauder basis property in the absence of local convexity.

title: The coanalyticity of the reduced K-theory on modules over free tensor algebras of dualizable t-categories
abstract: In this paper, we formulate Land-Tamme's $\boxtimes$-construction and $\odot$-construction for continuous exact monads on dualizable stable $\infty$-categories, and establish the behaviour of localizing invariants on pushouts of left modules over continuous exact monads on dualizable stable $\infty$-categories. Combining the Land-Tamme theory of continuous exact monads with the theory of analytic functors in Goodwillie calculus, we show that the reduced K-theory on modules over free tensor algebras of dualizable t-categories is modified 1-coanalytic or modified 2-coanalytic, depending on the coconnectivity of the base algebras. In particular, this answers Efimov's question concerning coanalyticity in the affirmative.

title: On $t$-designs supported by self-orthogonal codes
abstract: We study self-orthogonal $t$-$(v,k,λ)$ designs satisfying the condition that the codes generated by the designs are self-orthogonal codes whose codewords of minimum weight $k$ correspond to the blocks. A classification of such designs is given under the conditions that $t\geq \lfloor k/4\rfloor+1\geq2$ and $t \le 11$. This yields a classification of self-orthogonal codes of minimum weight $k$ whose codewords of minimum weight form a $t$-design under the same conditions.

title: Direct and indirect operator learning strategies for parametric optimal control problems
abstract: This paper focuses on the use of learning nonlinear operators via Deep Operator Networks (DeepONets) for approximating the solutions of optimal control problems. We study two operator learning strategies, namely, indirect and direct, both based on DeepONets, for parametric families of optimal control problems where the same problem must be solved many times for different initial data, different parameters, different cost function weights, and different bounds defining the set of the admissible controls. In the indirect strategy two DeepONets approximate the solution operators of the state and adjoint systems, and their predictions are used inside iterative projected gradient algorithms for finding the optimal control. In the direct strategy, a single DeepONet approximates the operator that maps directly to the optimal control generated by a reference solver; consequently, a new control is obtained through a single evaluation of the network. In order to analyze the computational cost, the efficiency, the speed and the accuracy of the learning strategies, we consider an optimal control problem related to an ordinary differential system that describes the temporal evolution of the glioblastoma growth subject to therapeutic interventions. For this specific optimal control problem we propose a discretize-then-optimize strategy, based on an implicit-explicit finite difference method, and then, we develop several numerical experiments in order to compare the two DeepONet learning strategies for this problem. The proposed operator learning DeepONet strategies can be adapted to approximate large classes of optimal control problems related to diverse differential systems.

title: Channel dichotomies
abstract: We study channel interconversion under non-signalling superchannels, where the asymptotic conversion rate is given by the ratio of the channel capacities. Our main result determines the second-order expansion of the optimal target length. Namely, when each channel has a single capacity-achieving dispersion, the coefficient is given by the inverse sesquinormal distribution, with parameters determined by the capacities and dispersions. The result extends state-dichotomy theory to channels: one superchannel approximates the target uniformly over inputs and maps every reference channel whose output is independent of its input to another such channel. As in state dichotomies, there are finite-error resonances where the second-order term vanishes, leaving an $O(\log n)$ remainder. Crucially, our new characterization cannot be obtained by concatenating channel coding and simulation protocols [Cao {\it et al.}~IEEE Trans.~Inf.~Theory (2024)]. Instead, the proof combines comparisons of binary hypothesis testing experiments with uniform Gaussian estimates and a construction that uses symmetry within type classes to satisfy the non-signalling constraints. Shared randomness assistance already suffices at first order, but we show that its second-order behaviour can differ strictly from the non-signalling case.

title: Bethe Hessian Recovery through the Kesten-Stigum Regime
abstract:
We show that outlier eigenvectors of the Bethe Hessian achieve weak recovery in the stochastic block model down to the Kesten-Stigum threshold, for every fixed common expected degree $d>1$. This extends previous recovery guarantees, which required $d$ to be sufficiently large. This threshold is information-theoretically optimal for the symmetric two-community model and is conjectured to mark the limit of efficient recovery in broader symmetric models. Our result matches the recovery guarantees of non-backtracking spectral methods while using Hermitian $n\times n$ matrices.
  To do this, we identify recursive formulas for the negative outlier eigenvalues and show that their eigenspaces have nonvanishing overlap with the corresponding planted eigenspaces. The proof constructs approximate eigenvectors from the planted labels on the limiting Poisson tree, with weights given by its Green's function, and transfers these approximations to the finite graph.

title: Lax-idempotent monads in homotopy theory
abstract: We extend the theory of lax-idempotent monads to the setting of $(\infty,2)$-categories. In particular, we prove an analogue of Kock and Zöberlein's characterization of the category of algebras over a lax-idempotent monad. We then apply this theory to many examples that arise naturally in homotopy theory. For example, we show that $(\infty,1)$-toposes are monadic over presentable $(\infty,1)$-categories, with left adjoint given by the symmetric $(\infty,1)$-topos. We also show that $\infty$-operads are comonadic over symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories through the monoidal envelope construction, obtaining along the way a new proof of Barkan-Steinebrunner's result that the envelope functor is a faithful inclusion. We furthermore use this theory to simplify Ramzi's proof that dualizable stable $(\infty,1)$-categories are comonadic over $\aleph_1$-compactly generated stable $(\infty,1)$-categories.

title: On reduced SPDE models for stochastic Cucker-Smale flocking dynamics
abstract: Flocking refers to a phenomenon in collective motion where particles align their velocities with each other, commonly modelled using Cucker-Smale dynamics. In this work, we introduce and analyse two general reduced SPDE models for stochastic Cucker-Smale particle dynamics that encompass environmental and i.i.d.-type noises. Our models are computationally cheaper alternatives to the underlying particle system and preserve the flocking behaviour. To derive our reduced models, we consider suitable empirical particle densities which depend on position and time, but feature velocity dependency in a multiplicative fashion: this setup crucially allows for a very intuitive and convenient notion of flocking at the SPDE level. In $d=1$ we prove flocking of the reduced SPDE models, and, for the environmental noise, we also quantify the discrepancy between the reduced SPDE and mollified particle system. We also discuss the technical modifications required to extend the results to higher dimensions. We then provide extensive numerical experiments to verify our theoretical results in $d=1$ and to explore the behaviour of our models in $d=2$.

title: Taylor-type joint spectrum and essential spectrum of row-bounded sequences of commuting operators
abstract: As the cornerstone of multivariable operator theory, (essential) Taylor's joint spectrum plays crucial roles in many areas. The present paper is devoted to developing the theory of (essential) Taylor-type joint spectrum of row-bounded sequences of commuting operators on Hilbert spaces and to establishing the associated Fredholm index theory. Furthermore, the holomorphic functional calculus for row-bounded sequences is established. At last, we obtain a Gleason-Richter-Sundberg type index theorem in the infinite-variable setting, which connects the Fredholm index, the asymptotic Arveson's curvature invariant and fibre dimensions.

title: Rates and Nearly-Lossless State over a Multi-Access Channel with Causal State Information
abstract: The problem of transmitting both data and state over a memoryless state-dependent multi-access channel with causal state information is addressed. The state comprises three independent components: a common component, which is revealed to both en- coders, and two private components, each of which is revealed to a different encoder. The data are to be recovered with arbitrarily-small probability of error, and the state sequence with arbitrarily-small symbol-error rate. Under the assumption that the capacity region in the absence of a state recon- struction constraint is nonempty, the capacity region is derived and is shown to be achievable using a Block-Markov coding scheme employing binning and superposition coding.

title: Improved estimation of differential entropy of a multivariate Gaussian distribution
abstract: We consider estimation of entropy of a multivariate variate normal distribution with unknown mean vector and unknown covariance matrix. Using a decision-theoretic approach, we study the problem under a general location-invariant loss function that is strictly convex and minimized at zero. We first characterize the class of affine equivariant estimators and obtain the best affine equivariant estimator. We further show that the best affine equivariant estimator is inadmissible under the general loss. Exploiting information in the sample mean, we derive Stein-type improved estimators, including an extension to the case of a mean matrix. Under the linex loss, we obtain a smooth Brewster--Zidek-type estimator that dominates the best affine equivariant estimator, and we show that this estimator is generalized Bayes under a suitable non-informative prior.

title: Holomorphic functions and hulls of Matsuki-dual orbits of $SU(p,q)$ in complex Grassmannians
abstract: Let $G_0$ be a real form of a complex semisimple group acting on a flag manifold $Z$, with maximal compact subgroup $K_0$ and its complexification $K$. Matsuki duality pairs each $G_0$-orbit $γ$ with a $K$-orbit $κ$, and $M=κ\capγ$ is a compact $K_0$-orbit. For lower-dimensional $γ$, $M$ is a compact CR manifold, and we ask which functions are holomorphic near $M$ and what its holomorphic hull is. In general, we show that $K_0$-finite holomorphic functions near $M$ are regular functions on $K$-orbits, and that $M$ carries non-constant holomorphic germs if some $K$-stable prime divisor of $Z$ misses $κ$, and, under a connectedness hypothesis, only constants otherwise. For $G_0=SU(p,q)$ acting on any Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}_k(\mathbb{C}^{p+q})$ we give a complete answer. Holomorphic functions near $M$ are constant unless $M$ is of holomorphic type: $k\in\{p,q\}$ and $M$ lies in the Harish-Chandra chart of the bounded symmetric domain $\mathcal{D}$. Then $M$ is the manifold of rank-$c$ partial isometries, and a holomorphic hull of $M$ is $\overline{\mathcal{D}}\cap\{\mathrm{rank}\le c\}$. This agrees with the polynomial hull of Kaup and Zaitsev except in one totally real case, where it is strictly smaller because $\det^{-1}$ is holomorphic near $U(p)$. The same dichotomy decides when global CR functions on $M$ are constant and when holomorphic sections of line bundles near $M$ are global; its exceptions differ from the Gindikin-Matsuki exceptions for cycle spaces, except at the base point of $\mathcal{D}$. This settles the descent question left open in earlier work with K. Shabbir on rank-one orbits. We also determine which $K$-orbits carry non-constant regular functions, prove constancy via chains of rational curves for small $c$, and compute Levi forms in examples.

title: Critical curl extremals and the hyperbolic plane
abstract: We study the critical Sobolev-curl quotient on $\mathbb{R}^3$ at the conformally invariant exponent $p=3/2$. Its sharp constant and optimizers were posed as open problems in the literature. We identify the toroidal and poloidal extremals. Two structural facts are used. First, the critical curl--curl equation is self-dual: the map $u\mapsto|\nabla\times u|^{-1/2}\nabla\times u$ is an involution on finite-energy solutions. It is the self-dual case of a duality between the exponents $p$ and $3p/(4p-3)$, which exchanges toroidal and poloidal fields and relates the sharp constants. Second, the toroidal minimization problem reduces exactly to a subcritical $3/2$-Laplace problem on the hyperbolic plane. Combined with symmetry and shooting results, these facts show that the two restricted sharp constants coincide. They also classify the gauge-minimal extremals: these are unique up to scaling and the Euclidean transformations realizing hyperbolic isometries, semi-explicit, and dual to each other. For nonzero one-signed profiles radial about a fixed hyperbolic centre, a gauge-canonical inverse of the duality yields an iteration by one-dimensional quadratures: the quotients are nonincreasing and converge to the restricted sharp constant, while the normalized iterates converge to the extremal pair. The first step from an explicit competitor gives the new upper bound $96\sqrt{15}π/(5\sqrt{4455π-13568})\approx11.2948$ for the restricted constants. The unrestricted sharp constant remains open. As an application, bounded axisymmetric poloidal potentials admit no $L^2$ zero mode of the Weyl-Dirac operator. An explicit conformal transformation extends this exclusion to both extremals at every real coupling.

title: Maximum edge overlap between independent random regular graphs
abstract: Optimising the vertex correspondence can substantially increase the number of edges shared by two independent realisations of the same random graph. We quantify this phenomenon for uniformly random $d$-regular graphs and derive corresponding results for their edge-based graph edit distance. For every fixed $d\geq 3$, we show that the maximum overlap is $n+Θ_{\mathbb P}(n/\log n)$, where the leading term $n$ arises from Hamiltonicity, while the surplus captures the optimal order of the excess beyond it. We establish explicit upper and lower bounds on the surplus. The upper bound is obtained by counting common cores of minimum degree at least two, while the lower bound is established using spanning factors consisting of cycles of the same logarithmic length. For the special case $d=2$, we show that the maximum overlap is $n-(1+o_{\mathbb P}(1))\log n$. The additional overlap achievable is also studied by rotating aligned Hamilton cycles, using a contiguity argument. As a by-product, we determine the asymptotic maximum overlap between unions of independent random perfect matchings under cyclic shifts.

title: Distributed Grid Search for Hyperparameter Tuning
abstract: The performance of many distributed optimization algorithms over peer-to-peer networks strongly depends on the choice of their hyperparameters. However, existing selection rules often require global quantities, yield conservative choices, or are tied to specific algorithms and hyperparameters. We propose Distributed Grid Search (D-GS), a consensus-based search method that evaluates and selects hyperparameter configurations across the network, requiring only the ability to run the tuned algorithm and evaluate local gradients. We also propose a zoom-in variant, Distributed Zoom Grid Search (D-ZGS), which improves empirical performance at a reduced cost. We prove that both methods terminate in finite time with all agents holding the same hyperparameter configuration, and quantify the (sub)optimality of this configuration. Numerical experiments on linear and logistic regression show that D-GS closely matches a centralized reference and that tuning and deployment cost a fraction of deploying algorithms with hyperparameters tuned using theoretical results.

title: Characterizations and MacWilliams-Like Identities of Weakly Regular Bent Partitions
abstract: Bent partitions play a significant role in the theory of bent functions. In this paper, we study weakly regular bent partitions, that is, all generated bent functions are weakly regular (called in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$). Let $Γ=\{A_{i}, i \in V_{m}\}$ be a bent partition of $V_{n}$ in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$, where $V_{n}$ denotes an $n$-dimensional vector space over the prime field $\mathbb{F}_{p}$, $n$ is even, $m \leq \frac{n}{2}$, and $m \geq 2$ if $p=2$. We first characterize bent partition $Γ$ in terms of the duals of component functions of vectorial bent functions. In particular, we prove that if $p \neq 3$, then all bent functions generated by $Γ$ are regular. Building on the above result, we give characterizations of bent partition $Γ$ in terms of two classes of linear codes. When $n \geq 4$ and $m=\frac{n}{2}$, except for the case where $(p, n)=(2, 4)$ and $|A_{i_{0}}|=1$ for some $i_{0}$, we show that $Γ$ is obtained from a spread (after a shift). Particularly, any normal bent partition of $V_{n}$ of depth $p^{\frac{n}{2}}$ in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$ must be obtained from a spread (after a shift), where $n \geq 4$. We establish the Macwilliams-like identities for bent partitions in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$. Furthermore, if $p$ is odd, we present some nonexistence results on bent partitions in class $\mathcal{WRBP}$.

title: Hereditary Approximation under Hilbertian Extension
abstract: In this paper, we prove that if a Banach space $X$ has the hereditary approximation property, then $X\oplus_2 H$ has the hereditary approximation property for every Hilbert space $H$. This answers a question of Johnson and Szankowski. In addition, if $X$ is also reflexive, then every closed subspace of $X\oplus_2H$ has the metric approximation property. The proof uses Grothendieck's characterization of the approximation property, a factorization of nuclear operators through quotients of $X$, and a nuclear perturbation of the coordinate projection on a closed graph.

title: $W^{1,p}$ error estimates of an IPDG and a class of HDG methods for the Poisson problem on convex polyhedral domains
abstract: This paper analyzes a symmetric interior penalty discontinuous Galerkin (IPDG) method, a hybrid mixed DG method, and two representative hybridizable discontinuous Galerkin (HDG) methods for the Poisson problem on convex polyhedral domains. For any fixed $ε\in (0,\frac{1}{2})$, we first derive optimal discrete $W^{1,p}$ error estimates for $2\leq p<\frac{1}ε$ by combining the interface Green's functions developed in \cite{lq2026} with the Fubini-type weighted estimates established in this paper. These error estimates lead to discrete $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup stability for $2\leq q<\frac{1}ε$, where $q$ is the conjugate number of $p$ such that $\frac{1}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1$. Using this stability result and a suitably constructed dual problem, we extend the optimal error estimates to $\frac{1}{1-ε}<p<2$ and subsequently establish the corresponding inf-sup stability for $\frac{1}{1-ε}< q<2$. Thus, both optimal discrete $W^{1,p}$ error estimates and discrete $W^{1,q}$-$W^{1,p}$ inf-sup stability hold throughout the range $\frac{1}{1-ε}<p<\frac{1}ε$, with $q=p/(p-1)$. Note that all of the aforementioned results are free of logarithmic factors and also hold on polyhedral meshes (except for the hybrid mixed DG method). Compared with the conforming finite element method (FEM), establishing such error estimates and inf-sup stability results for DG methods on convex polyhedral domains is more delicate because their analysis involves mesh-dependent norms. Consequently, the operator interpolation theory employed for conforming FEMs cannot be directly applied to DG methods. Finally, a numerical example is presented to illustrate the theoretical results.

title: Reduction numbers under flat extensions
abstract:
The reduction number of the maximal ideal of a localization (or even faithfully flat extension) need not
  increase under specialization. Nevertheless, for
  each fixed local ring the reduction numbers of the maximal
  ideals of all its localization have a finite common bound.

title: Distributed Zeroth-Order Composite Finite-Sum Optimization via Incremental Variance Reduction
abstract: We study decentralized composite finite-sum optimization over a fixed connected undirected network, where agents access local component functions through function evaluations and share a possibly nonsmooth convex regularizer. In this setting, standard two-point gradient estimators can retain nonvanishing variance at a solution, complicating their integration with gradient tracking. We propose Distributed Zeroth-Order Incremental Variance Reduction (Distributed ZIVR), which combines incrementally updated component-gradient estimates with a proximal gradient-tracking scheme. The method admits an implementation using a constant number of function evaluations per agent at every iteration, without intermittent full-component or full-coordinate refreshes. For convex smooth component functions and strongly convex local averages, we establish linear convergence up to a controllable finite-difference error. With the finite-difference radius chosen for the target accuracy, Chebyshev-accelerated mixing yields a per-agent oracle complexity of $\widetilde{O}(d(m+κ)\log(1/ε))$ for expected squared solution error $ε$, where $d$ is the dimension, $m$ is the number of components per agent, and $κ$ is the condition number. This matches the centralized ZIVR oracle bound, while the communication bound has only an inverse square-root dependence on the network spectral gap. Experiments on logistic and robust regression demonstrate rapid reduction of solution and consensus errors.

title: Tropicalization and Polyhedral Completions of Weyl Algebras
abstract: We construct weighted and polyhedral completions of the Weyl algebra over a complete nonarchimedean field and organize them into a structure sheaf on a polyhedral $G$-site. For discretely valued fields, we prove two-sided flatness for $Γ$-rational polyhedral completions, yielding exact base change for finitely generated $D$-modules. For compact integral polyhedra, we also construct finite-type integral models whose special fibers are toric face rings and describe the reduction of Gauss points in terms of toric strata.

title: A Fan-Type Theorem for Hamiltonian Berge Cycles in 3-Uniform Hypergraphs
abstract:
Let $H$ be a simple $3$-uniform hypergraph on $n\ge7$ vertices, and put $τ_n=\binom{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}{2}$. We prove that $H$ has a Hamiltonian Berge cycle if its $2$-shadow is $2$-connected, every pair at Berge distance two has an endpoint of hypergraph degree at least $τ_n+1$, and every pair of codegree one has both endpoints above $τ_n$. The distance-two threshold is sharp, and the order range cannot be extended to $n=4,5,6$. The proof separates two structural arguments. A low-degree endpoint of an extremal longest Berge path forces Hamiltonicity, independently of the order and the degree threshold. For high-degree endpoints, injective charging and its equality cases force pairs of codegree one that permit further rotations. The cases $n=7,8$ are settled by exhaustive verification, with a completeness proof and a second implementation using direct vertex--hyperedge cycle search.
  Keywords: Hamiltonian Berge cycle; Fan-type condition; 3-uniform hypergraph; longest-path rotation; exhaustive verification.

title: An Efficient Randomized Hierarchical Tucker Decomposition
abstract: We introduce randomized algorithms for computing the hierarchical Tucker decomposition of high-order tensors.
